summary: shopcli is a standard-library Python package whose Shop().run(script) runs a small inventory language (item.add/remove/list, price.set/get, report.stock/margin, plus 'repeat N:') and always replies with {ok, results, warnings, error}. Every failure becomes one Refusal record (closed code, message, path ending in '✗', where line/source, valid alternatives, hint, pasteable fix, host_name) built by an ordered suggester: namespace member, mined redirects (rm/delete/ls/inventory, count→qty), near spelling within max(1,min(3,len/3)) edits, then same name on another kind of value. RANGE warnings are raised at their line and folded with a count, and Python exceptions are translated to E_HOST while results and warnings produced before a failure are still delivered.

pattern_mapping.Refusal: shopcli/refusal.py: Refusal dataclass (code, message, path, where, valid, hint, fix, host_name) with to_dict()/replace(); built by shopcli/binder.py:_refuse, shopcli/engine.py:_execute/_unknown_command and shopcli/translate.py
pattern_mapping.Code list: shopcli/codes.py: CODES (eleven codes, one documentation sentence each), ERROR_CODES, WARNING_CODES, is_known; every code is exercised by a script in tests/test_codes.py
pattern_mapping.Suggester: shopcli/suggest.py: Suggester.for_command / for_option with the fixed order _in_known_namespace, _in_unknown_namespace, for_option; edit_distance (adjacent swap = 1 edit), budget, closest, nearest_first
pattern_mapping.Redirect table: shopcli/registry.py: COMMAND_REDIRECTS (rm, delete, ls, inventory), OPTION_REDIRECTS (count/amount/quantity→qty, title→name, price→value), RANGE_REDIRECTS, CROSS_KIND_FIX — one table owned by the registry
pattern_mapping.Translator: shopcli/translate.py: translate(error, where, spec, command) plus attribute_of/receiver_of; the engine wraps every handler call and maps any exception to E_HOST
pattern_mapping.Site tracker: shopcli/site.py: SiteTracker (enter/where) filled by Shop.run per line; every refusal and warning reads where from it
pattern_mapping.Warning folder: shopcli/site.py: WarningFolder groups by (code, line, message) and increments count; filled by engine._execute, rendered last in the reply
pattern_mapping.Binder / evaluator (the detecting layers: shopcli/parser.py (E_SYNTAX, E_DUPLICATE_OPTION, repeat), shopcli/binder.py (E_UNKNOWN_OPTION, E_ARG_MISSING, E_ARG_TYPE, E_ARG_RANGE, RANGE warnings), shopcli/commands.py (E_NOT_FOUND, E_ARG_RANGE for stock and zero price), shopcli/engine.py (Shop.run orchestration and reply)

notes_applied: Note 1 (mine redirects from transcripts): a literal redirect table for rm, delete, ls and inventory, each with a hint naming the concept and a ready fix; tests prove no edit-distance rule would produce these.

Note 2 (one fixed suggestion order, budget max(1,min(3,len/3))): implemented in that exact order in shopcli/suggest.py, with tests in tests/test_ordering.py showing a structural fact beats a near spelling and a redirect beats a near spelling; transposed letters count as one edit.
Note 3 (fixes are code, in the agent's names): every fix is rendered from the agent's own parsed values via shopcli/render.py, keeping their option order and quoting values with spaces.

Note 4 (one shape, one closed code list for every layer): parser, binder, handlers and host errors all return shopcli/refusal.py:Refusal; a host failure is E_HOST with the Python exception name in host_name, never as the code.
Note 5 (the path is part of the message): paths read 'report.margin(name=widget, cost=2) → ✗ price.get(widget)', and self-inserted steps are absent.
Note 6 (the line is in the agent's program): SiteTracker records the line number and the source line the agent typed, including the repeat line for repeated commands.
Note 7 (warn at the line, fold repeats): repeat 500 of a value above the usual range yields one warning with count 500 and line 1.
Note 8 (a warning that is usually wrong is worse than none): only one warning code ships — RANGE for qty above the usual 0–1000 — because a near-miss guess would fire on correct code.

Note 9 (deliver what was produced before the failure): results and folded warnings from the lines (and repeat iterations) before the failure are always in the reply; tests/test_delivery.py checks this.

Note 11 (test codes and fixes): tests/test_codes.py asserts the example table covers CODES exactly, and tests/test_fixes.py runs every redirect and every fix produced for 32 failing scripts in a seeded shop and requires it to bind.
Structure/Collaborations: one module per participant (refusal, codes, site+warning folder, suggester, registry-owned redirect table, translator) so the code list and the redirects exist exactly once.
tests: 90 unittest tests in 9 modules under tests/; last run: 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests' -> Ran 90 tests, OK (no failures).
chapter_feedback: Helped: the sketch (suggest / unknownMethod / translate / foldWarnings) and the Structure table translated almost one-to-one into modules, which made the participant mapping and the review order trivial.

Helped: the explicit budget max(1, min(3, len/3)) and the statement that 'crop' and 'drop' are one edit apart convinced me to keep mined redirects ahead of edit distance, and to add adjacent-swap counting only as a spelling detail.
Helped: note 11 changed the design — tests run every fix, which immediately caught two fixes of my own that did not bind (a dropped qty option and a fix built from an unterminated quote).

Misled: the chapter's E_NAMESPACE means 'the name exists in another namespace', but TASK.md lists it among required codes without that nuance; I had to decide that an unknown namespace falls under E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND while 'report.remove' or a bare 'add' is E_NAMESPACE. A sentence about the namespace typo case would settle it.

Misled: 'the same name on another kind of value' assumes value kinds (image vs array). In a key=value language there are no kinds, so I mapped kinds onto namespaces/options/verbs; that mapping is an interpretation, not something the chapter covers.

Left to guess: what a refusal's message should say when a suggestion exists — the chapter empties 'valid' in that case, which reads as a reply-shortening rule; I kept empty 'valid' for unknown commands with a fix but always list options/names for option and not-found refusals.

Left to guess: how much of a warning's context belongs in the reply (the chapter says warn at the line with a hint, but not whether the source text is included); TASK.md only requires line, count and hint, so the warning omits 'where'.
Left to guess: whether fixes may use placeholder text (e.g. <qty>); the chapter demands pasteable code, so when no sensible literal exists I set fix to None rather than invent one.
